summary: Unexpected flip in region pin precedence during control-plane maintenance causing intermittent eu->us egress and p99 latency spikes
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent spike in p99 latency over the last maintenance window. Traffic that should have remained pinned to eu-west was observed egressing to us-east for a small percentage of requests during a 15-minute window. Impact: Increased p99 from ~140ms to ~2.1s for ~4% of requests; affects model redwood/gpt-medium-2024; impacts production inference for multiple endpoints. Environment: prod tenant for Fjord Analytics (EU residency pin enabled; strict pin set with fallback to us-east on capacity). Observed window: 2026-03-12 18:12–18:27 UTC. Customer noticed higher token cost for egress and is concerned about data residency and latency SLAs. Expected behavior: All requests from EU region remain pinned to eu-west unless explicit capacity failover is triggered. During control-plane maintenance there should be no unilateral change in pin precedence for healthy nodes. Additional context: Customer uses custom routing policy with priority order [eu-west:primary, us-east:fallback] and a pin TTL of 12 hours. They reported no changes on their end and no deployments at the time. This ticket captures investigation and next steps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer tenant with strict residency pin to eu-west
2) Send sustained traffic that normally pins routing (500 rps) to the same model and route
3) Observe routing logs and latency SLOs during scheduled control-plane maintenance (2026-03-12 18:10 UTC window)
4) Check egress hop and route selection for sampled request IDs reported by customer
observed_behavior: Subset of requests (~4%) were routed to us-east despite active eu-west capacity; these requests show an extra egress hop and p99 latency jump to ~2.1s. Traces show route selection decision made in control-plane between two config reload events.
expected_behavior: Routing should honor existing pin precedence (eu-west primary) and only choose fallback when primary pools are flagged unhealthy or saturated per config. No ephemeral flips during control-plane config reloads.
logs: trace://redwood/trace/ae54f1b2 - trace shows route chosen us-east, control-plane decision log: 'pin_priority=eu-west; fallback=us-east; chosen=us-east; reason=control_plane_reload'
comments: 2026-03-12T18:40Z - Asha Patel (Support): Logged initial report, requested routing and trace IDs from customer. Asked for examples of request IDs and timestamps.

2026-03-12T19:02Z - Customer (Fjord Analytics - S. Meyer): Provided three request IDs and noted this happened during our scheduled maintenance window; we have strict residency requirement and want to understand why any egress to us-east occurred.

2026-03-12T19:25Z - Luis Gomez (SRE): Initial triage: pulled control-plane logs during window, saw config reload at 18:15:38Z correlating with chosen=us-east decisions for a small set of requests. Flags show primary pool as healthy. Escalating to Serving/Runtime team for hypothesis about transient preference flip.

2026-03-12T20:10Z - Elena Park (Serving Runtime): Noted that during control-plane reload we shipped a priority-change flag as 'unset' for a short interval which is interpreted by router as 'no explicit primary' and fallback logic picks nearest available (us-east) for balancing. Adding reproducer and unit test in PR 1142 to prevent unset->fallback behavior.

2026-03-13T09:14Z - Luis Gomez (SRE): Shared mitigations: 1) Confirmed we can mark eu-west pool as force-primary for customer until fix is deployed; 2) Suggested disabling control-plane config rollouts during customer SLA windows as temporary workaround.
2026-03-13T12:30Z - Customer (S. Meyer): Accepted temporary force-primary and requested ETA for permanent fix and confirmation on no data residency leakage during window.
2026-03-13T15:05Z - Asha Patel (Support): Confirmed we are tracking PR 1142; assigned to Serving Runtime for backport and small config guard. Will update customer when patch is scheduled for release.

2026-03-13T17:00Z - Elena Park (Serving Runtime): Patch merged to main; will be rolled to prod during next deploy (ETA 2026-03-14 03:00 UTC) with a canary in eu-west first. Posting runbook link for maintenance window exclusions.
investigation_notes: Control-plane log at 18:15:38Z shows a config-reload transaction where 'primary_priority' field was briefly absent in routed-config payloads delivered to some edge proxies.
Edge proxies interpret missing 'primary_priority' as 'no explicit primary' which triggers fallback policy that may prefer lowest-latency available pool (us-east).
Affected sample traces all have 'control_plane_tx_id=tx_20260312_181538' and share same config hash mismatch across proxies in two AZs in eu-west, suggesting partial rollout of the reload.
No evidence of capacity or health degradation in eu-west pools at the time; serving runtime metrics show normal QPS and low error rate for eu-west nodes.
Hypothesis: Atomicity bug in config publish path during maintenance allows brief 'unset' priority state to be delivered to some proxies; those proxies default to fallback selection logic.
Customer billing: Approximately 4% egressed cross-region for 15 minutes; finance impact estimated and customer notified.
resolution: Workaround applied: eu-west pool force-primary flag set for Fjord Analytics (completed 2026-03-13 09:30Z). Root-cause fix merged in PR 1142 to ensure priority fields never become unset during config reloads. Patch scheduled to roll 2026-03-14 03:00 UTC with canary in eu-west. Post-deploy will monitor p99 across tenant and confirm no further cross-region egress. Customer to be notified after successful canary. Follow-up: add a pre-reload validation to reject reloads that would temporarily unset residency fields; created a short delivery ticket for ops (INT-2140).
next_steps: 1) Roll patch in controlled canary (eu-west) and monitor for 24 hours
2) Reconcile egress billing delta with Finance and propose one-time credit for customer for the maintenance window
3) Update runbook to include a maintenance-exclusion toggle for strict-residency tenants
4) Confirm with customer once canary passes and close ticket
